meta.scope: Chile batch 4 — Regional expansion + poverty contrast. Northern mining region (Antofagasta) vs highest-poverty southern region (La Araucanía) + supporting regional nodes. Completes the homogeneity check.
meta.homogeneity_note: Same national framework (ENE, CASEN, INACER, IPI components). Capital and northern mining regions show lower income poverty; La Araucanía remains the highest-poverty region.

candidates.title: Región de Antofagasta — core statistical identity (northern mining)
candidates.description: Northern mining region, major copper and lithium production zone. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average. Strong labour-market participation relative to southern regions.
candidates.notes: Mining-specialised region. CASEN 2024 income poverty 16.4% (close to or below national). ENE recent unemployment ~7.2%. Hosts major copper operations and lithium activity in the broader northern corridor.

candidates.title: Región de La Araucanía — core statistical identity (highest-poverty contrast)
candidates.description: Southern region with the highest income-poverty incidence in the CASEN 2024 results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under higher marginalisation.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast region. CASEN 2024: income poverty 28.6% (highest among the 16 regions); extreme poverty 13.0%. ENE still produces regular labour-force estimates (recent unemployment ~7.8%). National survey infrastructure reaches the region fully; local independent statistical density is thinner.

candidates.title: Región de Valparaíso — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Central coastal region, second-largest population after the Metropolitana. Income poverty close to the national average.
candidates.notes: Intermediate region. CASEN 2024 income poverty 17.8% (slightly above national 17.3%). Useful bridge between the capital and the extremes.

candidates.title: Región del Biobío — core statistical identity
candidates.description: South-central region with significant industrial and forestry activity. Income poverty moderately above the national average.
candidates.notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 19.3%. Completes a central–south transect alongside Valparaíso, Maule and Araucanía.

candidates.title: CASEN — pobreza por región (income and multidimensional)
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
candidates.description: Official regional tabulations of income poverty and multidimensional poverty from the CASEN survey. Primary source for the inter-regional poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2024 ranking (income poverty): Magallanes 9.9%, Metropolitana 13.3%, Antofagasta 16.4%, Valparaíso 17.8%, Biobío 19.3%, Los Ríos 22.3%, Maule 24.3%, Ñuble 23.9%, La Araucanía 28.6%.

candidates.title: ENE — resultados Región de Antofagasta
candidates.description: Regional cut of the National Employment Survey for the northern mining region.
candidates.notes: Recent moving quarter: unemployment ~7.2%, participation relatively high (~65%). Informal employment lower than in southern agricultural regions.

candidates.title: ENE — resultados Región de La Araucanía
candidates.description: Regional cut of the National Employment Survey for the highest-poverty southern region.
candidates.notes: Recent moving quarter: unemployment ~7.8%. Agriculture and public services are important employment absorbers. Demonstrates that the national labour survey reaches the high-poverty region with usable frequency.

candidates.title: INACER — Indicador de Actividad Económica Regional (multi-region)
candidates.description: Regional economic activity indicators produced for the 16 regions. Geographic counterpart to the national short-term activity measures.
candidates.notes: Allows comparison of short-term activity across mining, capital, central and southern regions under a common methodology.

candidates.title: Región de Magallanes y de la Antártica Chilena — low-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Southernmost region with the lowest income-poverty incidence in CASEN 2024. Completes the geographic poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 9.9% — lowest of the 16 regions. Small population but useful as the opposite pole to La Araucanía.

candidates.title: Región del Maule — secondary high-poverty node
candidates.description: Central-south agricultural region with elevated income poverty (second-highest after Araucanía in recent CASEN).
candidates.notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 24.3%. Reinforces the central–south poverty gradient alongside Ñuble and La Araucanía.

proposed_edges.basis: Regional poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national CASEN.
Antofagasta labour results are the regional cut of the national employment survey.
La Araucanía labour results are the regional cut of the national employment survey.
Regional activity indicators share the INACER methodology.
Antofagasta is a major geographic locus of copper (and lithium) production.
La Araucanía’s high poverty ranking is derived from the CASEN regional tabulations.
